findings.text: Rule strategies lead to date: rule.model_news_double.v1 30 trades, 21 wins, net 803.29 USD (2.68%); rule.model_news_global.v1 12 trades, 11 wins, 647.57 (5.4%). Nearly all of it came this week (double: 23 trades, net 862.86), when base.always_up.v1 also earned 2651.26. A rising week for long-only rules, not proven skill.

One-parameter comparisons with the reference rule.model_news.v1 (14 trades, 1.54%): calm 4.19% (9 trades), confirmed 3.36% (11), high 2.35% (10), half -1.16% (6). base.model_only.v1, news off, lost -214.98 on 4 trades. Samples of 4-14 largely shared trades prove nothing yet; rule.model_news_strict.v1 is absent from the tables.

ai.pattern_mood.sonnet.v1, the only AI trader with a real sample, has 69 trades, 36 wins, net 285.24 (0.41%), near base.momentum.v1 (583 trades, 0.05%). ai.combined.sonnet.v1 has 6 trades, ai.combined.opus.v1 1 (CAT, -44.68); ai.news_results.sonnet.v1 is absent from the tables. Too few to rank AI traders.

The week's biggest wins and misses came from company-specific moves with no counted news (GM up, CAT down); GOOGL's falls were mostly news and sector. Their exits finished outside the published range, so the ranges were too narrow for these single-name moves.

Some cells' intervals exclude zero: promotional medium analyst items -0.6654% at 2 days (126 events) and -1.3803% at 5 (108); unverified high earnings items +0.8261% at 4 days and +1.6383% at 5 (110). Uncorrected intervals over hundreds of cells, events overlapping across horizons, one week: no edge shown. Verified earnings items: 1 event each, not enough.
